items.claim: Do not load client certificates into the process-wide default SSLContext. In one process, `requests.get(url_a, verify=True, cert=(certA, keyA))` runs and then `requests.get(url_b, verify=True)` (or a call with a different cert on another thread) runs against a server that asks for a client certificate.
items.consequence: urllib3 calls `context.load_cert_chain()` on the supplied `_preloaded_ssl_context`, so client A's identity stays installed and is presented on later verify=True requests that pass no cert, and concurrent requests with different certs race on one context. Against a local mTLS server the head shows `['clientA', 'clientA', 'clientB', 'clientB']` where the merge-base shows `['clientA', None, 'clientB', None]`.
items.proposed_fix: In `_urllib3_request_context`, pass the shared context only when `client_cert is None`; otherwise set `pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` so urllib3 builds a private context for that pool as before.

items.claim: Keep an adapter's own TLS context and settings when verify=True. An `HTTPAdapter` subclass whose `init_poolmanager` passes `ssl_context=` (or `ssl_version=`, as in `docs/user/advanced.rst`) to `PoolManager` is mounted and used with the default verify=True.
items.consequence: Per-request `pool_kwargs["ssl_context"]` overrides the manager's `connection_pool_kw`, so the custom context is never used; cipher or protocol restrictions and legacy-server workarounds silently stop applying. `adapterctx.py` shows `uses custom ctx: False` at the head and `True` at the merge-base.
items.proposed_fix: In `_get_connection`/`_urllib3_request_context`, skip adding `ssl_context` when the adapter's pool or proxy manager already defines one in `connection_pool_kw`, and keep the previous CA-bundle handling in that case.

items.claim: Load the default CA bundle lazily, not when requests.adapters is imported. The certifi bundle path is missing or unreadable, for example a distro-patched certifi in a minimal container or a frozen app without `cacert.pem`.
items.consequence: `import requests` raises `FileNotFoundError`, so programs that only use http, verify=False or an explicit bundle break, and the 'Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle' message is lost; at the merge-base import succeeded and the error appeared on the first verify=True request. Every import also pays the bundle-parsing cost.
items.proposed_fix: Build and cache the default context on the first verify=True request, guarded by a lock, instead of at module level.
